newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran reiterates sees no need to raise OPEC ceiling.
newsitem.headline: Iran reiterates sees no need to raise OPEC ceiling.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh reiterated on Tuesday that OPEC should act "cautiously" in setting its output ceiling for 1997 and that raising the ceiling would be "not wise", the official IRNA news agency reported.
Aghazadeh told Reuters last week in Ankara he did not believe there was a need for the producer group to raise its ceiling during ministerial talks scheduled in Vienna later this month.
Aghazadeh told IRNA that "the OPEC ministers should not take the favourable oil market conditions of 1996 as a yardstick in their forthcoming meeting," the news agency reported.
OPEC ministers will be meeting in Vienna to set the group's output ceiling for at least the first six months of next year.
Gulf sources and OPEC delegates have said it is unlikely that the group will change its ceiling of 25.003 million barrels per day (bpd) in Vienna.

Aghazadeh highlighted higher output from non-OPEC countries, the possible return of Iraq to world oil markets and uncertainties over the winter weather as factors mitigating a cautious attitude by OPEC states.
"The minister also said that violation of quotas by certain OPEC members has created problems for the organisation," IRNA reported.
